title: Simple dictionary
description: Create a HashMap<String,String> with 5 Spanish words and their English translation. Allow the user to search for a word and show its translation.
hints: Use diccionario.put("gato", "cat") for each word pair
Use diccionario.get(palabra) to search the translation
Check with containsKey() whether the word exists before showing it
solutionExplanation: A HashMap is created and 5 key-value pairs are added with put(). To search, containsKey() checks whether the word exists and get() obtains its translation.

title: Frequency counter
description: Count the frequency of each letter in a text using a HashMap<Character, Integer>. Show the result sorted by descending frequency.
hints: Use texto.charAt(i) to access each character
Use containsKey() to check whether the letter is already registered
With getOrDefault(letra, 0) + 1 you can simplify the increment
solutionExplanation: Each character of the String is iterated. Spaces are ignored. For each letter, getOrDefault() obtains the current frequency (0 if it does not exist) and it is incremented by 1 with put(). Then the map is iterated with entrySet() to show the results.

title: Group by category
description: Given a HashMap<String, String> of products and their categories, group the products by category using a HashMap<String, ArrayList<String>> and show the result.
hints: Iterate over the original HashMap with entrySet() or keySet()
If the category does not exist as a key, create a new ArrayList
Use getOrDefault(categoria, new ArrayList<>()) or containsKey() to initialize
solutionExplanation: The product HashMap is iterated and each product's category is obtained. If the category is not yet a key in the grouped map, a new ArrayList is created for that category. Then the product name is added to the corresponding ArrayList.
expectedOutput:
Ropa: [Camisa, Pantalón]
Electrónica: [Laptop, Mouse, Auriculares]
Calzado: [Zapatillas, Sneakers]
